summary.intent: Land three output-identical core performance optimizations (F3, F4, F10 from the perf analyst's report) as a PR on the caliper repo, delegated to a subagent and then published by the main session.
summary.outcome: The subagent implemented F3, F4 and F10 in one signed commit on perf/core-merge-dedupe, verified byte-identical output against origin/main and passing checks; the main session then linked trail #382, found draft PR #446, and wrote its title and body. The PR shows BLOCKED on Entire Gates, and CI has not been checked.

repo: Perf changes in core are validated by byte-identical `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` output versus an origin/main release build, with `stats` dropped, using the analyst's same.py and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-core/identity.sh.
Identity matrix is gate-large and chakra-only, default and --no-checker, with and without `--load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none` (8 pairs).
Check suite for PRs: just lint, doc-check, machete, typos, deny, semver, test-rust, test-checker-lane, and test-parity (construct:parity recipe).
PRs are linked to Entire trails via `entire trail link <n> --branch <b> --base main --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper`; PR then shows BLOCKED on Entire Gates until findings/gates resolve.
The exports map only feeds a DashMap, so its iteration order is not observable and no order test is needed; export_of is covered through layers by existing tests.
#445 and #440 conflict in 8 files; recommended merging #440 first.

code.finding: SourceSyntax::read now skips union props whose parent Arc pointer was already seen and file names already seen (by &str); files still inserted in first-seen order so `wanted` iteration is unchanged.
loader.exports.into_read_only() (O(1)) replaces into_iter().collect(), which re-hashed the whole map single-threaded (~14 ms, ~20% of a --no-checker run); read site uses .iter().
replace_props collects props into a Vec and builds the map in one pass; a repeated name still keeps the later prop.

workflow: When wall time is unreliable under high load (load avg ~15, ±0.4 s swings), use instructions retired as a stable proxy for comparing variants.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions; the main session verified the remote SHA via git ls-remote before publishing the PR.
Be explicit in PR bodies about what was not verified (analyst ms gains, quiet-machine A/B, allocation counts).

friction: Machine was heavily loaded by other workers (load ~15), making wall-clock benchmarking useless.
PR #446 is BLOCKED on Entire Gates and CI status was not inspected.
